question: A sales manager wants to see which of their sales reps have logged the most calls this month. Which report type should they use?
explanation: The Tasks and Events report type allows you to report on activities including calls, meetings, and tasks across all users.
whyWrong: Activities with Accounts and Accounts with Activities focus on account-related activities, not standalone tasks/calls across reps.
Activity History is a related list on records, not a report type for building reports.

question: What is the maximum number of fields that can be tracked for field history on a custom object?
explanation: You can track up to 20 fields per object for field history tracking on both standard and custom objects.
whyWrong: 10, 15, and 25 are not the platform limit; the documented maximum per object is 20.

question: A user needs to create a report that shows Opportunities grouped by Account and then by Stage. Which report format should be used?
explanation: Summary reports allow you to group rows of data, view subtotals, and create charts. They're ideal for grouping by Account and then by Stage.
whyWrong: Tabular reports show flat rows only; they do not support grouping or subtotals.
Joined reports combine multiple report types and are not the primary format for simple grouping by Account and Stage.
Matrix reports are for row and column grouping (e.g. cross-tab), not hierarchical grouping by two dimensions.

question: Which permission allows a user to transfer records they don't own?
explanation: The 'Transfer Records' permission allows users to transfer records they don't own to other users.
whyWrong: View All grants read access to all records, but viewing isn't the same as being able to transfer ownership.
Modify All grants full edit/delete access on all records of an object, but doesn't specifically grant transfer rights over records you don't own.
Edit only lets a user modify records they already have access to — it doesn't grant the ability to transfer ownership of records they don't own.

question: What happens when a Workflow Rule with a Time-Dependent Action is triggered, but the record no longer meets the rule criteria before the action executes?
options: The action is removed from the queue
explanation: Time-dependent actions are removed from the queue if the record no longer meets the workflow rule criteria when the action is scheduled to execute.
whyWrong: Time-dependent actions that no longer apply are silently removed from the queue rather than triggering an error log entry.
The action doesn't execute anyway — Salesforce re-evaluates the record against the rule criteria at execution time and skips the action if it no longer qualifies.
No automatic admin notification is generated when a time-dependent action is removed for no longer meeting criteria.

question: Which record-triggered flow trigger is used when you need to perform actions before the record is saved?
explanation: Before Save flows run before the record is committed to the database, allowing you to modify field values or perform validation.
whyWrong: Platform Event isn't a record-triggered flow timing option — it's a separate trigger type based on event messages, not before/after save timing.
After Save triggers run after the record is committed to the database — too late to modify field values before save.
After Delete triggers run following a delete operation, unrelated to modifying a record before it saves.

question: What is the purpose of a Permission Set in Salesforce?
options: To grant additional access to users without changing their profile
explanation: Permission Sets extend user access by granting additional permissions, object access, and app access without modifying the user's profile.
whyWrong: Validation rules enforce data quality logic — they're unrelated to what Permission Sets do.
Permission Sets don't replace profiles — every user still needs exactly one profile; permission sets layer additional access on top.
Page layouts are configured separately from Permission Sets — layouts control field/related-list display, not access grants.

question: Which feature allows users to customize their Home page layout with different components?
explanation: Lightning App Builder can be used to customize the Home page, allowing users to add and arrange components.
whyWrong: Validation rules enforce data entry rules — they have nothing to do with Home page layout customization.
Record types control which picklist values and page layouts are available for a record — they don't customize the Home page layout.
Profiles control overall access and settings, but customizing the Home page layout is a separate Lightning App Builder capability, not a profile setting.

question: What does a Campaign Influence report help sales managers track?
options: Which marketing campaigns influenced opportunities and closed revenue
explanation: Campaign Influence reporting shows how marketing campaigns contributed to opportunity creation and closed revenue.
whyWrong: Email open rates are a Marketing Cloud/Pardot-level metric, not what Campaign Influence reports on within core Sales Cloud.
Campaign Influence tracks more than spend — it connects campaigns to the opportunities and revenue they contributed to.
Lead source counts are a separate reporting dimension — Campaign Influence specifically links campaigns to opportunity outcomes, not just lead counts.

question: Which Case assignment rule criteria type allows assigning cases based on multiple conditions?
explanation: Case assignment rules support both rule criteria (field-based conditions) and formula criteria for complex logic.
whyWrong: 'Rule criteria only' undersells the actual flexibility — assignment rules can also use formula-based criteria for more complex conditions.
'Formula only' excludes the simpler rule-criteria option that's also available — both mechanisms exist side by side.
Manual assignment is the fallback when no rule matches — it isn't itself a rule criteria type.

question: What is the primary purpose of Queue-based case routing?
options: To group cases for teams to work from a shared list based on skills or workload
explanation: Queues allow cases to be routed to teams rather than individuals, enabling workload balancing and skill-based routing.
whyWrong: Queues organize records for teams to work from — they aren't a reporting tool.
Queues can trigger notifications, but that's a secondary feature, not their primary purpose.
Queues aren't a deletion mechanism — they're a routing and collaboration mechanism for shared work.

question: Which object is required to enable Products, Price Books, and Opportunities in Salesforce?
explanation: Products and Price Books must be configured to enable the full opportunity-to-quote-to-order sales process.
whyWrong: Lead is a separate object in the sales process, unrelated to enabling Products and Price Books on Opportunities.
Campaign tracks marketing campaign data — it isn't required to enable Products, Price Books, and Opportunities functionality.
Opportunity itself doesn't need to be 'enabled' via a separate object — Product and Price Book is the actual object relationship that must be set up to use products on opportunities.

question: What does the 'View All' permission on an object allow?
options: View all records in the org regardless of sharing rules
explanation: View All bypasses sharing rules and allows the user to see all records of that object in the organization.
whyWrong: 'Delete all records' is part of Modify All, not View All — View All is read-only.
'Transfer all records' is a separate specific permission, not what View All grants.
'Edit all records' describes a different, broader permission (Modify All) — View All doesn't grant edit access.

question: Which report format displays data in rows and columns with subtotals at the intersection?
explanation: Matrix reports use both row and column grouping, with subtotals at the intersection of rows and columns.
whyWrong: Tabular reports list rows in a simple flat list without any grouping or subtotals at row/column intersections.
Joined reports combine multiple report types side by side — they don't specifically provide the row/column subtotal grid Matrix does.
Summary reports group rows and show subtotals along one dimension, not intersecting rows and columns.

question: What is the purpose of Chatter Groups in Salesforce?
options: To enable collaboration and discussions around projects, topics, or teams
explanation: Chatter Groups allow teams to collaborate, share files, and discuss work in a centralized feed.
whyWrong: Chatter Groups aren't a reporting feature — that's a distinct Salesforce capability.
Chatter Groups don't handle case assignment — that's managed by assignment rules and queues, not Chatter.
Chatter Groups don't replace email — they're a separate, complementary collaboration channel.
